subject: Concurrency surge, tail errors and proportional remedy request
messages:
From: Alan Torres <ops@clearline.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected 503s and queue drains during peak — can you confirm impact window?

Hi David,

We started seeing a spike of 503s and backend queue drains during Clearline's peak between 2026-11-30 22:05 UTC and 2026-11-30 22:28 UTC. Our checkout rate briefly doubled and several requests failed with 503 / connection-reset, plus increased retry amplification.

We attached a short log snippet and the top-level request ids we correlated (clearline-req-*) — can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood observed a concurrent surge on your side at that window?
- If so, whether this qualifies for SLA remediation under our contract (monthly availability SLO)?
- What evidence you can provide (raw traces / trace ids) and an ETA for a postmortem?

We flagged this to our ops and billing teams — billing@clearline.com is cc'd. This incident materially impacted our checkout success rate for ~23 minutes; we need to initiate the remedy process if eligible.

Thanks,
Alan Torres
Ops Lead, Clearline Payments

Attachments: clearline_request_log_snippet.txt (txt stub)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alan Torres <ops@clearline.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:03:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected 503s and queue drains during peak — can you confirm impact window?

Alan — thanks for the heads up and for the log snippet. I've started an internal trace collection and looped in Laura (AM) and Karthik (platform eng).

Immediate next steps from Redwood's side:
- Karthik: collect raw trace bundles + kernel-level telemetry for the 22:00-22:40 UTC window and check for preemption/eviction events.
- I'll preserve the tenant-level telemetry and mark this as an SLO review candidate.
- Laura: will coordinate a customer-facing postmortem and any provisional credits after engineering confirms eligibility.

Could you also share any traffic shaping changes or client-side retry spikes on your end? That will help us determine if the root cause was routing/queuing within our serving layer versus upstream traffic pattern changes.

We expect to have an initial impact verification within 8 business hours and a postmortem invite by EOD tomorrow.

—David
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 16:21:47 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected 503s and queue drains during peak — root-cause notes (prelim)

Folks — quick summary of what the serving telemetry shows for Clearline tenant during the 22:05–22:28 UTC window:
- We observed a short concurrency surge across multiple frontend instances that coincided with an aggressive autoscaler step-down in the regional pool.
- The concurrency burst caused an accelerated KV cache eviction pattern; several shards experienced high eviction rates and elevated latencies while rebuilding.
- Three frontends experienced transient rejection (503) during KV-cache warmup. The frontend logs show preemption/eviction warnings and a set of retry spikes that align with Clearline request ids.

Evidence collected (attached as a small bundle):
- prelim_trace_bundle.tar.gz (contains top-level trace ids and a 5MB sampling of spans)
- kv-eviction-heatmap.png (eviction density for the region)

Prelim impact assessment: the behavior looks like a platform-induced tail latency event caused by a combination of autoscaler timing + cache warmup. That maps to an availability degradation on our side and could be eligible for a proportional remedy under the contract — but we need legal/contract to confirm the exact entitlement calculation.

Asks:
- Legal/Prod Ops: confirm whether a proportional (prorated) credit applies for a 23-minute regional availability gap under CL-8921.
- CS/AM: prepare a customer-facing postmortem with a plain-language explanation and mitigation plan (canary thresholds, cache warmup improvements).

I'll continue to pull full raw traces and an ordered timeline; sending the bundle now.

—Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachments: prelim_trace_bundle.tar.gz (stub), kv-eviction-heatmap.png

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alan Torres <ops@clearline.com>; David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, billing@clearline.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 14:40:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood action plan and proposed remedy for 2026-11-30 window

Hi Alan — thanks for raising this and for patience while we pulled telemetry. We have a short customer-facing plan and proposed remedy we want to run by you: 

What happened (plain language): during your peak on 2026-11-30 we saw an unexpected concurrency spike that coincided with autoscaler activity in the region. That led to cache rebuilds on a few frontends and transient 503s while caches refilled. Engineering has confirmed this was on Redwood's serving stack.

Proposed immediate remediation:
- Postmortem meeting: Wed 2026-12-03 15:00 UTC — invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=postmortem-meeting-20261202
- Evidence we will provide: full trace bundle, ordered event timeline, and GC/kernel telemetry for the impacted hosts.
- Remedy proposal: a one-time, proportional credit equal to 10% of Clearline's average daily invoice for November 2026 (we estimate this is ~USD 4,200). Alternatively we can apply a token-based credit if you prefer account-level balance.

Next steps for Clearline: please confirm whether the proposed credit is acceptable and if you want the postmortem meeting. If billing needs a formal invoice adjustment, Laura will loop Legal/Finance to generate a remediation memo.

If acceptable, we will: schedule the postmortem, finalize the trace bundle, and ship a remediation memo within 5 business days.

Sincerely,
Laura Bennett
Account Director, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
